answer: Anchor each agent identity to a unique registered domain name: the agent publishes its public key in a DNS TXT record, checked each epoch. A reef of fake identities needs a fresh domain per clone, and each registration costs money, leaves a WHOIS trail, and takes time to propagate. Sybils stand on a narrow ledge: bulk creation is expensive and traceable, and dozens of domains sharing one registrar or payment card are easy to flag. If a domain lapses, the identity dies, so an attacker must keep paying rent per fake. Even sable-deep budgets cannot sustain a thousand-clone swarm.
